content:
maria: Heads up — we need a clear policy for span routing + privacy redaction before GA. Current fanout duplicates spans and spikes retention/costs for some tenants.

sam: Quick Q — where do we want the rewrite to happen: collector/router or exporter layer?

maria: Router-level rewrite would avoid sending PII to vendors, but exporters expect different attr sets (tempo wants full traces, honeycomb wants stripped).

lee: We do rewriter-in-exporter today which means if we fanout to multiple backends we mutate per-exporter and end up storing multiple variants. Costly.

nina: Could we rewrite once upstream and keep an internal-only copy (hashed id) for debugging under auth? Compliance might object.

jamal: Alternate: add a routing_hint tag on spans, perform a single-pass redact/keep decision, then route copies. That way we don't do full re-write per-exporter.

ryan: Example config I sketched:
```
route:
  match:
    org: "payments"
  send_to: [tempo, honeycomb]
  sampling:
    priority_high: keep_all
    default: 0.01
  redact:
    fields: ["user.email","payment.card"]
```

sam: That looks fine but the console needs to present these rules as structured objects, not raw YAML. Also we need schema validation.

maria: Quotas: per-tenant span rate + burst token bucket. If quota exceeded -> fallback to aggregated exports (counts only) to Datadog + emit metric for dropped spans.

nina: UX: console should show per-route cost estimates for 7/30/90 day retention and projected monthly bill. Also flag high-risk fields that will be redacted.

jamal: Operationally we need graceful fallback: if Tempo ingest is slow, route lower-priority traces to honeycomb or aggregated sink. That requires routing policy with priority weights.

lee: Performance worry: routing+rewrite adds latency. We should measure p50/p95 impact and KV cache hit ratio. If we add a sync rewriter we'll regress. Suggest async rewriter where possible.

maria: For compliance customers (Private), we must support an option: "no external copy" which forces single-sink routing.

ryan: ops-bot: created INF-2146 for the console cost panel mock :ticket:

deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: eng-platform-prod -> feature/telemetry-routing at 2025-11-12T03:00:00Z

jamal: Rollout plan: feature flag + 1% tenants smoke -> 10% if cost delta < 10% and p95 latency delta < 20ms -> full. Add auto-rollback on cost spike.

nina: We also need a migration story for existing per-tenant exporter configs; translate them to new route objects and surface diffs in the console.

sam: Internal API debate: keep a dedicated "router" microservice vs embed routing in the collector. Router service gives more flexibility (policy eval, rate limiting) but is another hop. Collector-level is cheaper latency but harder to iterate. Thoughts?

lee: Prefer router service behind a fast IPC link to collector. That balances iteration and perf. We'll prototype with gRPC and measure.

maria: Action items: (1) finalize policy schema & validation (maria) (2) spike single-pass rewrite + gRPC router (lee) (3) console cost mock + migration UI (nina) (4) quota sim + cost model (jamal) (5) telemetry panels for p50/p95 & dropped spans (ryan)

sam: I'll own the schema docs and an RFC draft. Will ping infra for storage choices (dynamo vs postgres).

maria: OK I'll open the RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/telemetry-routing and link the PR.

ryan: I'll add dashboards and alerts: p95 latency for router, span-drop-rate, route-cost burn rate.

jamal: Tests: unit for rewriter, integration with tempo+honeycomb mocks, e2e with canary flow.

maria: Thanks — let's sync in eng-platform sync on Friday to review the spike output. :thumbsup:
